messages:
maya: Heads up — seeing 3–5% pod-to-pod packet loss across eu-west1 GPU clusters after last night's CNI rollout (cilium 1.25.2 -> 1.25.2+rev3). High tail gRPC latency and intermittent RDMA handshake timeouts. @oncall

sam: I can confirm on grafana: embeddings-service p99 latency jumped 250ms -> ~2.1s right around the rollout window. Packet drops timeline lines up with the deployment. https://grafana.internal/r/ABc123

deploy-bot: deploy finished: cilium-control-plane v1.25.2 -> v1.25.2+rev3 at 2026-03-17T23:10Z (rolled by infra-rollout) :white_check_mark:

alex-sre: grabbed tcpdump from gpu-eu-03 between two pods on different nodes. seeing a lot of ICMP "fragmentation needed" + repeated retransmits on overlay. snippet below (filtered):

```
15:23:44.123456 IP 10.40.5.12 > 10.40.6.33: UDP, length 1400
15:23:44.123457 IP 10.40.6.33 > 10.40.5.12: ICMP frag needed and DF set, mtu 1450
15:23:44.123458 IP 10.40.5.12 > 10.40.6.33: UDP, length 1400 (DF) (retransmit)
```

jordan: kernel logs show RDMA qp create errors and a bunch of "GSO segment count mismatch" warnings. looks like an offload<>tunnel MTU interaction. example from dmesg: `rdma: ib_create_qp failed -EINVAL`

nina: If this is an encap path MTU/offsload regression we should decide: rollback cilium in eu-west1 only (canary) or patch iptables/tunnel flags. Rolling back to previous cilium build is fastest but has ops cost and possible config churn. thoughts?

sam: Quick checks to run if anyone else hits this: 1) iperf3 pod->pod, 2) iperf3 host->host, 3) `ethtool -k <tunnel-if>`, 4) `ip link show` to verify MTU on vxlan/geneve/cilium_netdev.

maya: ran iperf3: host->host looks fine (10G, ~9.5G, 0.2% UDP loss). pod->pod via cilium_vxlan path shows ~3.8% UDP loss and increased jitter. ethtool on tunnel shows GSO: on, TSO: on, GRO: on. MTU on cilium_vxlan0 is 1404 (we set that for encap).

alex-sre: pasted outputs we collected:

```
# ip link show cilium_vxlan0
4: cilium_vxlan0: mtu 1404 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default 
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
# ethtool -k cilium_vxlan0
Features for cilium_vxlan0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
large-receive-offload: on
```

jordan: suspect path: host offload (GSO/TSO) is producing segments larger than tunnel MTU and ip stack/kernels on some nodes drop or send ICMP frag-needed with DF set. RDMA stack is sensitive to these latent drops leading to handshake failures.

nina: mitigation options: 1) rollback canary in eu-west1-gpu immediately; 2) force-disable GSO/TSO/GRO on tunnel interfaces as a short-term kernel-level mitigation and monitor; 3) apply iptables rule to clamp MSS/DF on encapsulated flows. Each has tradeoffs: (1) safest for correctness, (2) perf hit and CPU overhead, (3) targeted but fiddly and risk of missing flows.

sam: I can script the GSO disable and MSS clamp for canary nodes if we want to test before rollback. commands to try (quick):

```
# disable offloads on tunnel on node
ip link set dev cilium_vxlan0 down
ethtool -K cilium_vxlan0 tso off gso off gro off
ip link set dev cilium_vxlan0 up
# clamp MSS on FORWARD chain (example)
iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp -m tcpmss --mss 1405:65535 -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400
```

maya: start canary rollback plan for eu-west1-gpu only. I'll roll back the cilium deployment for the GPU nodepool and keep non-gpu clusters on the new version. Nina, can you coordinate rollback window with infra-schedule and notify product/CS?

nina: ack. scheduling 30m canary rollback window, notifying stakeholders now. patching ops playbook with the GSO toggle as fallback.

oncall-bot: paging oncall: trigger sent to @eng-oncall. See incident: INC-2026-032-eu-west1-cni

alex-sre: canary rollback started — reverting cilium-control-plane on eu-west1-gpu nodes. Monitoring grafana.

maya: update: 20m after rollback, pod->pod packet loss down to ~0.4% and embeddings p99 back to ~260ms. RDMA handshake errors not seen since rollback.

jordan: leaving note: we need a postmortem on offload+encap interactions and an automated test that exercises large-packet RDMA flows through the overlay during upgrades.

nina: agreed. I'll book a follow-up postmortem and add a checklist: (1) validate tunnel MTU vs host PMTU for each node, (2) smoke RDMA flows, (3) test GSO/TSO permutations in canary job.

maya: thanks all — keeping this thread open for logs and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
